sentences.text:
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 13019 of 2022
Applicant :- Amit Sagar

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Rakesh Kumar Verma
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mrs. Jyotsna Sharma,J.
1.

Heard Sri Rakesh Kr. Verma, learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and
perused the record.

2. The instant anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with a prayer to
release him on bail in Case Crime No. 865 of 2022, u/s 376, 120-B I.P.C., P.S. Majhola, District
Moradabad.

3.  As per the allegations in the F.I.R., the marriage of the first informant was settled with the instant applicant Amit Sagar; the ceremony for 'god bharai' was solemnized and both the sides exchanged gifts; the marriage was postponed as the applicant was preparing for some examination; in 2021, the applicant was appointed as a clerk in an inter college in Lakhimpur Kheri; the first informant/victim went there and stayed for three days with him; the applicant, on assurance of marriage, established physical relations with the victim, however, thereafter he kept on postponing the marriage function and in the end he declined to marry her.
4. It is contended on behalf of the applicant that the 'god bharai' ceremony was, in fact, solemnized in 2018; but owing to some disagreements and disputes, the marriage could not materialize.

Both the parties settled the matter by entering into a written compromise on 18.4.2022 (paper No. 23);
some disputes remained which were again settled by entering into another compromise on 20.7.2022.

sentences.text:
My attention has been drawn to both the papers on which the signatures of the first informant,
the applicant and other members of family are present, to stress the point that whatever were the disputes between the two, have been settled and both the parties withdrew from the proposed relationship and also returned the gifts which were exchanged earlier and that no grievances were left on any of the sides.
6.
It is further contended that for some ulterior motives, this false F.I.R. has been lodged by adding twisted and distorted facts and to further harass the applicant.
7. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail.
However, the copy of the compromise papers as aforesaid have not been denied.

8. In case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that while deciding anticipatory bail, Court must consider nature and gravity of accusation, antecedent of accused, possibility of accused to flee from justice and that Court must evaluate entire available material against the accused carefully and that the exact role of the accused has also to be taken into consideration.

entities.text: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. In the instant case, I considered submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances.
In my view, a case for anticipatory bail is made out.
Hence, the present anticipatory bail application is allowed.

sentences.text: In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court below shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

12. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion at any stage of the case based on material before him.
